name: weather_shadow_visibility
_comment: §13a: a cloudy-day shadow has to be visible, not merely computed.
moon_shadow_render reads MatBases.SunShadow.color.r — the FINAL composed shadow colour the
shader draws with, Color.Lerp(white, colors.shadow, alpha). Its name is from §6a but the value
is the general one, and it is the only measurement that distinguishes 'the alpha is right' from
'you can see a shadow' — which is exactly the distinction this fix is about.
Noon at latitude 20 so the sun is high and ShadowIntensityFromElevation has saturated; the alpha
is then governed by weather alone. Expected values computed offline from WeatherDimmingMath.
The A/B toggle is weather_dimming, because §13a is gated on it: with §13 off, vanilla's flat
0.92 is the only weather softening there is and the patch deliberately stands down.

steps._comment: Clear noon is the reference and must be untouched: the patch substitutes Clear's OWN colour, so on Clear it is a no-op by construction. 0.718 is vanilla's skyColorsDay.shadow.
Rain at noon with §13 OFF — the patch stands down, so this captures the shipped artifact: vanilla's flat 0.92, an 8% darkening that no correct alpha can reach past.

Rain at noon with §13 ON — the fix. Cloud opacity is 1.0 (every non-Clear vanilla weather shares one skyColorsDay), so alpha is ShadowContrastFactor(1.0, MaxDimming) and the colour is now Clear's 0.718. On the shipped Cinematic preset (maxDimming 0.20) that is alpha 0.4333 -> rendered 0.8778, a 12.2% darkening against the 3.5% it used to be.

Fog and a hard blizzard read identically to Rain — same skyColorsDay, so same opacity. Probed to PIN that, not to celebrate it: §13a does not make weathers differ from each other, and a future change that thinks it did should fail here.
Night must be untouched: §6a's Patch_MoonShadowColor owns colors.shadow below the horizon and §13a stands down there. Hour 2 on a clear night with the moon up reads §6a's own value.
